transcript:
Meeting Header:
Date/Time: 2025-09-30 16:00 PT
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Evan Park (Redwood CSM), Marta Ruiz (Solstice - Procurement), David Chen (Solstice - CISO), Aisha Thompson (Solstice - Legal), Ravi Patel (Solstice - Platform), Olga Ivanova (Solstice - PM)

[00:00] Jordan Lee: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'll kick us off. We wanted to walk through the MSA/DPA status, SLA questions, and the onboarding steps so procurement and legal have what they need to sign.

[00:12] Marta Ruiz: Thanks Jordan. We got the initial MSA back from procurement and marked up a few items. Aisha is on to go through the legal points but high level procurement wants to confirm data residency and liability caps.

[00:25] Aisha Thompson: Yes, we have three big items: one, liability cap language - we usually prefer 1x annual spend; two, data residency and subprocessors; three, termination assistance and data return methods. Also concerned about audit rights.

[00:41] Jordan Lee: Totally fair. High level - Redwood generally proposes a 1M USD cap or 1x annualized fees for enterprise - we can discuss which fits. For data residency, we support region pinning for Dedicated and Private deployments. For hosted accounts there are region controls but not a hard guarantee unless you go Dedicated/Private.

[00:58] David Chen: So for PHI and ePHI flows, we need to ensure processing is in the US only. We're looking at a hybrid model - some workloads will be in our VPC, some via hosted API. Is that right?

[01:12] Priya Nair: Correct. If you need strict US-only, Dedicated or Redwood Private (VPC) is the path. We also have contractual DPA clauses around subprocessors and we can add a schedule listing the major cloud providers we use. Note - sometimes the transcription tool calls it "Redwood Pri-vate" - but it's Redwood Private.

[01:30] Aisha Thompson: On subprocessors - can we get a commitment to notify within 30 days of adding new subprocessors?

[01:37] Evan Park: We can commit to notification of major changes; our standard DPA has a notice period; 30 days is reasonable, we'll confirm exact language in the DPA redline.

[01:48] Ravi Patel: From an engineering perspective, we need to understand key management - can we use our KMS? Are keys customer-managed for Private?

[01:56] Priya Nair: Yes, for Redwood Private you can bring your own KMS/HSM. For Dedicated we support KMS integration; for hosted there are SaaS-managed keys but we offer envelope encryption and integrations with major KMS providers on enterprise plans. We'll attach the KMS integration matrix in the security packet.

[02:15] Olga Ivanova: Great, also curious about SLAs - uptime and latency SLOs. Our product has a hard latency requirement for interactive clinical workflows.

[02:24] Jordan Lee: For Dedicated we offer SLA-backed throughput and latency targets. Typical SLA is 99.9% for availability on Dedicated clusters with credit calculations tied to minutes downtime. For hosted, we publish performance profiles but SLA for latency is limited; we recommend Dedicated for strict latency requirements.

[02:39] Marta Ruiz: What's the SLA credit calculation look like? Is it a simple pro-rata refund or service credit?

[02:45] Priya Nair: It's service credits. Our MSA has a schedule with defined thresholds - for example, availability below 99.9% but above 99.0% yields X% credit; below that yields higher credits. We'll send the exact SLA schedule; procurement typically wants the numeric table which we'll include.

[03:00] David Chen: Can we request an additional remediation step for severe incidents, like priority post-incident review and specific runbook access?

[03:09] Evan Park: Yes we can include escalation matrices and post-incident reviews for Dedicated customers - that's part of our enterprise support add-on. We'll outline that in the support appendix.

[03:23] Aisha Thompson: Liability cap again - do you have flexibility on higher caps for healthcare customers?

[03:28] Jordan Lee: We can consider higher caps in negotiated enterprise contracts tied to committed spend. For pilot/proof-of-concept we usually stick to our standard cap but as you move to a committed Dedicated contract we can discuss increasing the limit.

[03:40] Marta Ruiz: Regarding pricing approval - our finance team needs an MOQ and monthly commit options. Can you send commit tiers?

[03:47] Priya Nair: Absolutely. We'll send the Dedicated capacity commit options: monthly and annual, with burst credits and headroom. I'll include example pricing for the 3-, 6-, and 12-month commit levels.

[03:59] Ravi Patel: For pilot we're planning a small Dedicated pool to test clinical flows. We'll need to run benchmarks for steady-state QPS and tail latency. Who runs the benchmarks?

[04:08] Priya Nair: We typically run a joint benchmark: Redwood SEs will run and collect metrics, and we can provide an artifact spreadsheet with token-level latency and cost. We'll need your sample prompt sets and expected concurrency.

[04:22] Ravi Patel: We'll share a representative prompt set and expected concurrency - around 60 concurrent users, average request size ~300 tokens.

[04:29] Jordan Lee: Good. We'll include an onboarding checklist in Slack/shared folder.

[04:36] Marta Ruiz: On audit rights - we need to perform periodic audits or at least review audit evidence. Do you provide SOC 2 Type II and penetration test results?

[04:44] Evan Park: Yes - we have SOC 2 Type II and can share the report under NDA. We also have pen-test summaries and a security package. I'll post links after the call.

[04:52] David Chen: Any concerns about model hallucinations and data leakage? For PHI we need to ensure we don't train on customer data.

[04:59] Priya Nair: We don't train Redwood-hosted models on customer data. For Dedicated and Private deployments, customer data never leaves your environment. We'll add explicit language about training restrictions in the DPA/contract.

[05:12] Aisha Thompson: Termination assistance - we want a clear export process and vendor cooperation for a transition period.

[05:18] Jordan Lee: Standard is 30 days termination assistance with data export in machine-readable format. We can extend that for enterprise customers; we'll propose options in the MSA redline.

[05:29] Marta Ruiz: Good. Procurement also asked about cyber insurance requirements and indemnities for regulatory fines.

[05:36] Jordan Lee: We'll provide our standard indemnities and confirm cyber insurance details. Often customers require carriers and limits - we can supply our certs.

[05:44] Olga Ivanova: For onboarding timeline, if legal signs by mid-October can we start pilot by late October? We need at least two weeks for integration.

[05:52] Jordan Lee: Yes, that's feasible. If we get signed MSA/DPA and required access, we can kick off a 2-week pilot the following week; SEs will schedule a technical kickoff.

[06:05] Marta Ruiz: Aisha, any last legal items?

[06:08] Aisha Thompson: I'll review the redlines but mainly want the DPA subprocessors list and KMS language. Also want clarity on breach notification timelines - 72 hours is what we expect.

[06:18] Evan Park: Our standard is 72 hours for breach notification; we'll confirm in writing.

[06:23] Ravi Patel: A few technical clarifications - for Dedicated, is prefix KV cache available and can we warm caches during ramp? Also what's the expected cold-start latency?

[06:33] Priya Nair: We support KV/prefix caching in the runtime, and we can pre-warm during onboarding. Cold-start depends on model size and hardware; typical cold-start for a 13B model on Dedicated is on the order of tens of seconds for container warm; but with pre-warming we get interactive latencies. We'll include a performance doc with typical numbers.

[06:51] David Chen: Regarding data residency again - can you add a contractual clause that processing of PHI will only occur in the specified region for Dedicated and Private?

[06:59] Jordan Lee: Yes, we can add a region-pinning clause for Dedicated/Private, we'll propose language in the DPA.

[07:07] Marta Ruiz: Okay reminder to procurement - we'll need the final pricing and MSA redline by next week to route for approval.

[07:14] Jordan Lee: Recap and next steps: Jordan will send the redlined MSA/DPA summary and marked documents by 2025-10-02; Priya will share Dedicated pricing tiers and SLA schedule by 2025-10-03; Evan will post SOC 2 and security artifacts by 2025-10-01; Ravi to send prompt set and concurrency numbers by 2025-10-06. Jordan will propose pilot kickoff dates after MSA is accepted.

[07:35] Aisha Thompson: Sounds good, we'll review and get back with any additional redlines.

[07:39] Jordan Lee: Thanks everyone. We'll follow up in email.

[07:43] End of recording

Notes: Transcript includes some auto-transcription quirks; product names occasionally mistranscribed (e.g., "Redwood Dedicate"), acronyms sometimes expanded incorrectly. References shared during call: dedicated-pricing.xlsx (link sent in chat), security-package/soc2.zip (link to S3 placeholder), MSA_redlines_2025-09-30.docx (to be shared).
